CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFGRIDUPDATE

CFGRIDUPDATE goes in the action page of a form that contains a CFGRID in SELECTMODE="EDIT". It compares the submitted cells with their original values and runs the matching UPDATE, DELETE and INSERT statements against one table.

Category

Forms

Syntax

<CFGRIDUPDATE GRID="grid_name"
    DATASOURCE="ds_name"
    TABLENAME="table_name"
    KEYONLY="Yes/No"
    DBTYPE="type"
    USERNAME="user"
    PASSWORD="password"
    TABLEOWNER="owner"
    TABLEQUALIFIER="qualifier">

Attributes

GRID
Required. NAME of the CFGRID whose data was submitted.
DATASOURCE
Required. Data source that holds the table.
TABLENAME
Required. Table to update. The grid's column names must match the table's column names.
KEYONLY
Optional, default "Yes". Yes: the WHERE clause of UPDATE and DELETE uses only the table's primary key. No: it also requires every other grid column to still hold its original value, so a row someone else changed in the meantime is left alone.
DBTYPE
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
USERNAME
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
PASSWORD
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
TABLEOWNER
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
TABLEQUALIFIER
Optional. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.

Usage

The key is the table's PRIMARY KEY column(s); a table without one is keyed on its first column. Include the key in the grid (hidden with CFGRIDCOLUMN DISPLAY="No" or read-only with SELECT="No").

For every row, a checked "Del" box produces a DELETE; changed cells produce one UPDATE with only the changed columns. A filled-in insert row produces an INSERT of its non-empty cells. Rows that were not touched are not sent to the database at all. If a statement fails (a duplicate key, say), a Database exception is thrown.

The DBSERVER, DBNAME, PROVIDER and PROVIDERDSN attributes of other drivers are accepted and ignored too.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- The edits go to a scratch copy of Departments that is dropped at
      the end, so the sample data never changes. --->
<CFSET Scratch = "GridDemo" & RandRange(1000, 9999)>
<CFQUERY DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
CREATE TABLE #Scratch# (Dept_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Dept_Name VARCHAR(30), Location VARCHAR(40))
</CFQUERY>
<CFQUERY DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
INSERT INTO #Scratch# (Dept_ID, Dept_Name, Location)
SELECT Dept_ID, Dept_Name, Location FROM Departments
</CFQUERY>

<CFIF IsDefined("Form.FieldNames")>
  <CFTRY>
    <CFGRIDUPDATE GRID="DeptGrid" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" TABLENAME="#Scratch#">
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Any">
    <CFOUTPUT><P><B>Update failed:</B> #CFCATCH.Message#</CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
  </CFTRY>
  <CFQUERY NAME="After" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
  SELECT * FROM #Scratch# ORDER BY Dept_ID
  </CFQUERY>
  <P>After <B>CFGRIDUPDATE</B> the copy holds:
  <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=2>
  <CFOUTPUT QUERY="After">
  <TR><TD>#Dept_ID#</TD><TD>#Dept_Name#</TD><TD>#Location#</TD></TR>
  </CFOUTPUT>
  </TABLE>
</CFIF>
<CFQUERY DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">DROP TABLE #Scratch#</CFQUERY>

<CFQUERY NAME="GetDepts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT Dept_ID, Dept_Name, Location FROM Departments ORDER BY Dept_ID
</CFQUERY>
<P>Edit, tick "Del" or fill in the yellow row, then save:
<CFFORM NAME="Depts" ACTION="cfgridupdate.cfm">
<CFGRID NAME="DeptGrid" QUERY="GetDepts" SELECTMODE="EDIT"
    INSERT="Yes" DELETE="Yes" WIDTH="420">
  <CFGRIDCOLUMN NAME="Dept_ID" HEADER="ID" SELECT="No">
  <CFGRIDCOLUMN NAME="Dept_Name" HEADER="Department">
  <CFGRIDCOLUMN NAME="Location" HEADER="Location">
</CFGRID>
<INPUT TYPE="Submit" VALUE="Save changes">
</CFFORM>
